questions.q: How should you keep utility class order consistent?
options: Use the official Prettier plugin to sort classes

questions.q: What does the container query variant @md: respond to?
options: The width of the nearest @container ancestor, not the viewport
questions.explain: Components adapt to the space they get.

questions.q: What does rtl: help with and what is better?
options: Direction-specific overrides; prefer logical utilities such as ps-4 and ms-auto that adapt automatically

questions.q: How do you theme several brands with the same components?
options: Components use semantic tokens (such as bg-brand) whose variable values are switched per scope

questions.q: What should you check when a class does not apply?
options: That it appears as a complete string in a scanned file, then inspect the generated rule in DevTools

questions.q: What shows a Tailwind design system is production-ready?
options: Accessibility and visual-regression tests in CI, documentation and a versioned release process

challenges.title: A responsive card: classes and the CSS they generate
challenges.prompt: Write the class list for a card (rounded, white, padded, shadowed; a row from the md breakpoint with a gap; gray hover and dark-mode backgrounds), then build it with the Tailwind v4 CLI and read the utilities layer of the generated CSS. The expected output below is the generated utilities layer from a real build; compare the order of rules and the shape of the variants.
challenges.explain: Each class becomes one rule; variants wrap or qualify the selector (a media query for md:, :hover inside @media (hover: hover), and a prefers-color-scheme query for dark:). Verified by compiling the classes with Tailwind CSS v4.3 and printing the utilities layer.

challenges.title: Design tokens, a custom utility and a custom variant
challenges.prompt: Define theme tokens, a custom breakpoint and spacing base in @theme, add a custom utility with @utility and a custom variant with @custom-variant, then compile classes that use them. The expected output shows the generated utilities and the theme variables Tailwind kept because they were used.
challenges.explain: Variables in @theme become real CSS custom properties and generate matching utilities (bg-brand, 3xl:p-8); @utility and @custom-variant add your own. Only the variables actually used are emitted, and p-4 is now calc(var(--spacing) * 4) with the 0.5rem base. Verified by compiling with Tailwind CSS v4.3.
